USMLE-style practice · Pathology

A clonal source of amyloid

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 69-year-old woman develops nephrotic-range proteinuria, orthostatic symptoms, and an enlarged tongue. Biopsy confirms amyloid. Serum testing shows an abnormal free light-chain ratio, and bone marrow contains a clonal plasma-cell population. Which precursor most likely forms her deposits?

  1. Immunoglobulin light chain
  2. Serum amyloid A
  3. Beta-2 microglobulin
  4. Transthyretin
  5. Islet amyloid polypeptide
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Immunoglobulin light chain

The combination suggests AL amyloidosis; a plasma-cell clone produces the light-chain precursor. Tissue typing is still needed to confirm the amyloid type.

Understanding the options

Immunoglobulin light chain
The combination suggests AL amyloidosis; a plasma-cell clone produces the light-chain precursor. Tissue typing is still needed to confirm the amyloid type.
Serum amyloid A
SAA produces AA amyloid in chronic inflammation rather than a light-chain-producing clone.
Beta-2 microglobulin
This precursor is associated with long-term dialysis and osteoarticular disease.
Transthyretin
TTR amyloid commonly causes cardiomyopathy or neuropathy but is not produced by plasma cells.
Islet amyloid polypeptide
IAPP deposits are typically localized to pancreatic islets.
